Home / Parts for Ford F-LINE road trucks

Parts for Ford F-LINE road trucks

The road segment is part of the F-LINE family from Ford Trucks. A parts request for a distribution or haulage truck is checked against the chassis configuration and the vehicle's equipment.

Send the part number for filters, brakes, suspension, steering, engine or cab. If the vehicle also has body equipment, name its manufacturer separately; chassis parts and equipment parts are identified separately.

Which parts you can request

Engine and lubrication, filters, brakes, clutch and driveline, steering, suspension, cooling, electrics, cab and identified body components.

Send the details, we identify the part

The VIN helps for the truck itself. For mounted equipment we also need the equipment manufacturer's details.

Request a quote

We do not list part numbers whose fitment for this version is unconfirmed. Send the vehicle details for an individual check.

Model name: official Ford Trucks documentation. EKS LKW is an independent supplier.

FAQ

Can I request a part for a Ford F-LINE road truck without a part number?

Yes. Send the VIN, a description and a photo. For body equipment, add its make, model and serial number.

Are the parts genuine or aftermarket?

You can ask for either. The manufacturer, part number and fitment are stated in the quote.

Do you have every part in stock?

We do not publish stock online. Availability and sourcing are confirmed per request; for most parts the usual lead time is 12–48 hours, confirmed in the quote.

Can I also request body parts?

Yes, on request, once the manufacturer and configuration are identified. Equipment components are not treated as Ford parts by default.

Useful details for Ford F-LINE road truck parts

The Ford F-LINE road series covers trucks with several axle configurations. The Ford Trucks range includes models such as 1833 DC, 2533 LR and 2633 HR. When you request a part, write the full model name from the papers or the truck's plate and tell us what the vehicle is used for.

For a service, list the consumables you are replacing and mark which numbers you copied from the fitted parts. If the workshop noted the engine model or an earlier part number, include it. We check every item before confirming the quote. You can request engine, cooling and fuel parts separately.

For electrical or lighting faults, show the part marking, the connector and where it is fitted. For a rear lamp, note the side and send a photo of the connector. For a sensor, say which assembly it is fitted in. The full number helps most when housings look alike.

For driveline or axle parts, look for the assembly's plate. Photograph whatever is readable and say where the part was removed from. If you have a list for several trucks, group the numbers by vehicle so it is clear where each item goes. Add quantities and priorities next to each number.

If a truck needs to get back on the road, tell us when you need the part and the delivery town, so the team can give you the options available. The chassis number helps when the part name is too general. You can also start from a number on an invoice, as long as you say where it came from.

If you send several photos, keep them in the same order as your parts list.

FAQ

Can I send a list for several F-LINE trucks?

Yes. Split the list by vehicle and give the part number, quantity and position for each item.

What do I send if an electrical part has no label left?

Send photos of the connector, the housing and where it is fitted, plus the truck's full model name.
